arxiv-2106-01256.title: Quasiconformal almost parametrizations of metric surfaces Thanks: Research supported by Swiss National Science Foundation Grant 182423.
arxiv-2106-01256.creator: Damaris Meier, Stefan Wenger
arxiv-2106-01256.description: Abstract . We look for minimal conditions on a two-dimensional metric surface X X of locally finite Hausdorff 2 2 –measure under which X X admits an (almost) parametrization with good geometric and analytic properties. Only assuming that X X is locally geodesic, we show that Jordan domains in X X of finite boundary length admit a quasiconformal almost parametrization.

arxiv-2204-00089.description: Abstract Existing works have identified the limitation of top- 1 1 attack success rate (ASR) as a metric to evaluate the attack strength but exclusively investigated it in the white-box setting, while our work extends it to a more practical black-box setting: transferable attack.

arxiv-2302-06426.creator: Miguel Ortega-Martín, Óscar García-Sierra, Alfonso Ardoiz, Jorge Álvarez, Juan Carlos Armenteros, Adrián Alonso
arxiv-2302-06426.description: Abstract Linguistic ambiguity is and has always been one of the main challenges in Natural Language Processing (NLP) systems. Modern Transformer architectures like BERT, T5 or more recently InstructGPT have achieved some impressive improvements in many NLP fields, but there is still plenty of work to do.

arxiv-2405-17183.title: Exact Thermodynamics For Weakly Interacting Normal-Phase Quantum Gases: Equations of State For All Partial Waves
arxiv-2405-17183.creator: Xin-Yuan Gao, D. Blume, Yangqian Yan
arxiv-2405-17183.description: Abstract While the thermodynamics for bosonic systems with weak s s -wave interactions has been known for decades, a general and systematic extension to higher partial waves has not yet been reported. We provide closed-form expressions for the equations of state for weakly interacting systems with arbitrary partial waves in the normal phase.

arxiv-2407-16937.title: A converse to a theorem of Gauss on Gauss sums

arxiv-2501-06449.description: Abstract Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a transformative technology for 6G networks, enabling the seamless integration of communication and sensing functionalities. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), with their capability to adaptively reconfigure the radio environment, have shown significant potential in enhancing communication quality and enabling advanced cooperative sensing.

arxiv-2504-20325.title: Gaussian tripartite steering in Schwarzschild black hole
arxiv-2504-20325.creator: Shu-Min Wu 1 , Hao-Yu Wu 1 , Yu-Xuan Wang 1 , Jieci Wang 2
arxiv-2504-20325.description: Abstract Multipartite steering is a fundamental quantum resource that is uniquely suited to tackling complex relativistic quantum information challenges, but its properties in the gravitational field context remain to be elucidated. We study the distribution of Gaussian tripartite steering in the background of a Schwarzschild black hole.

arxiv-2509-05057.title: Radiation damage to the Hubble Space Telescope during two Solar cycles, and correction of Charge Transfer Inefficiency 2025 Radiation damage to the Hubble Space Telescope during two Solar cycles, and correction of Charge Transfer Inefficiency – References
arxiv-2509-05057.creator: Richard Massey, Jacob A. Kegerreis, Juan Paolo Lorenzo Gerardo Barrios, James W. Nightingale, Richard G. Hayes, David Lagattuta, Zane D. Lentz, Gavin Leroy, Jesper Skottfelt, Maximilian von Wietersheim-Kramsta
arxiv-2509-05057.description: Abstract From 2002 to 2025, the Hubble Space Telescope’s Advanced Camera for Surveys has suffered in the harsh radiation environment above the protection of the Earth’s atmosphere. We track the degradation of its image quality, as Solar protons and galactic cosmic rays have damaged its photosensitive charge-coupled device (CCD) imaging sensors.

arxiv-2601-17325.title: Bounds on Linear Turán Number for Trees
arxiv-2601-17325.creator: Rajat Adak, Pragya Verma
arxiv-2601-17325.description: Abstract A hypergraph H H is said to be linear if every pair of vertices lies in at most one hyperedge. Given a family ℱ \mathcal{F} of r r -uniform hypergraphs, an r r -uniform hypergraph H H is ℱ \mathcal{F} -free if it contains no member of ℱ \mathcal{F} as a subhypergraph.

pmc-11417327.creator: Chun-Kang Lee, I-Chieh Chen, Hsueh-Ju Lin, Ching-Heng Lin, Yi-Ming Chen
pmc-11417327.description: BackgroundSerum uric acid (SUA) is an important predictor of cardiovascular events and mortality. The ABCG2 rs2231142 variant (TT genotype) is associated with hyperuricemia (HUA), but the relationship between ABCG2 gene polymorphisms and coronary artery disease (CAD) risk is poorly elucidated.

pmc-11481669.title: Evaluating the impact of treatment sequencing on outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma: a comparative analysis of TACE and systemic therapies
pmc-11481669.creator: XingRong Zheng, Xin Song, BoXiang Zhang, XiYao Chen, YeQiong Zhang, QiuMin Luo, ZhiPeng Li, ZheXuan Deng, RuiXuan Xu, Liang Peng, Chan Xie
pmc-11481669.description: This study aimed to evaluate how the timing of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) relative to systemic therapy (tyrosine-kinase inhibitors [TKIs] and immune checkpoint inhibitors [ICIs]) influences oncological outcomes in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). A retrospective analysis was conducted on HCC patients treated with TACE plus TKIs and ICIs from January 2018 to February 2023.

pmc-11554798.title: Beyond Conventional Treatments: Exploring CAR-T Cell Therapy for Cancer Stem Cell Eradication
pmc-11554798.creator: Lobna E Rabie, Ahmed A Mohran, Kholoud A Gaber, Nour M Ali, Asmaa M Abd El Naby, Eman A Ghoniem, Basmala A Abd Elmaksod, Ahmed N Abdallah
pmc-11554798.description: BackgroundFor decades cancer remained the center of attention in the scientific community as its survival rates are low. Researchers from all around the world wanted to know the core of the problem as to what initiates cancer in a patient and helps with its progression.

pmc-12715846.title: Adaptive neuromodulation dialogues: navigating current challenges and emerging innovations in neuromodulation system development
pmc-12715846.creator: Frederik Lampert, Matthew R Baker, Michael A Jensen, Amir H Ayyoubi, Christian Bentler, Jessica L Bowersock, Rosana Esteller, Jeffrey A Herron, Graham W Johnson, Daryl R Kipke, Christopher K Kovach, Vaclav Kremen, Filip Mivalt, Joseph S Neimat, Theoden I Netoff, Enrico Opri, Alexander Rockhill, Josh
pmc-12715846.description: Adaptive neuromodulation systems and implantable brain-computer interfaces have made notable strides in recent years, translating experimental prototypes into clinical applications and garnering substantial attention from the public. This surge in interest is accompanied by increased scrutiny related to the safety, efficacy, and ethical implications of these systems, all of which must be directly addressed as we introduce new neurotechnologies.

pmc-13136507.title: Physical Therapy Intervention With Hippotherapy (HPOT) Affects Balance Control in the Elderly: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-13136507.creator: Bita Bahrami Gholami, Ali Fatahi, Neda Boroushak, Rozhin Molavian
pmc-13136507.description: Background and AimsAging is characterized by a decline in functional abilities, strength, balance, flexibility, agility, and coordination due to neurological and muscular changes. Hippotherapy (HPOT) has been recognized for its physical and psychological benefits for older adults. Hence, this study aimed to investigate the effects of hippotherapy on balance in elderly individuals.

pmc-13227214.title: Training for complexity: Fostering interdisciplinary thinking in One Health graduate education
pmc-13227214.creator: Kristen Sullivan, Meredith R Spence Beaulieu, Jade Lyons, Emily Floess, Alexandria P Nelson, Caitlin G Niven, Savanna K Smith, Chenxing Xie, Michael Reiskind
pmc-13227214.description: Graduate training in One Health must equip students to think across disciplines and address complex health challenges through integrative approaches. While case-based and project-based learning are increasingly used to support these goals, there is limited research on how graduate students engage in interdisciplinary exchange, particularly through peer feedback.

pmc-13287890.title: 6: Characterization of tropomyosin receptor kinase signaling in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
pmc-13287890.creator: Georgios Koulios, Ting-Fang Lee, Kevin C Ray, Vincent Quoc-Huy Trinh, Frank Revetta, M Kay Washington, Kemal M Akat, Daniela Sia, Youngmin A Lee
pmc-13287890.description: BackgroundTropomyosin receptor kinases (TRK) TRKA, TRKB and TRKC (encoded by NTRK1, NTRK2 and NTRK3, respectively), regulate survival, proliferation and differentiation of neurons through ligand-dependent activation of downstream signaling pathways including MAPK, PI3K and PKC. TRK-fusion positive cancers have ligand-independent activation of TRKs and have emerged as potent oncogenic drivers that can be very effectively targeted by FDA-approved TRK inhibitors.

pmc-13366001.title: IFPHPOS0026 Mental and Physical Health Outcomes of Informal Caregivers: A Systematic Review
pmc-13366001.creator: Danielle Varley, Rebecca Jones, Anne-Marie Bagnall
pmc-13366001.description: IntroductionInformal caregiving involves providing short- or long-term support for a family member, partner, friend, or neighbour with a disability, illness or injury. While frameworks have been developed to support informal caregivers, informal caregivers are typically unaware of the support available and are not trained or adequately equipped to undertake strenuous tasks, leading to negative physical and mental health outcomes.

pmc-13367297.title: Intravenous Lipid Emulsion Therapy for Severe Emamectin Benzoate Poisoning: A Case Report
pmc-13367297.creator: Ahmed A Al-Adhroey, Mohammed A Al-Mahdi, Ahmed Y Al-Waisi
pmc-13367297.description: Emamectin benzoate poisoning is an uncommon but potentially life-threatening cause of neurocardiovascular toxicity. We report the case of a 22-year-old man who presented with coma, respiratory failure, and refractory shock after intentional ingestion of emamectin benzoate. Conventional supportive measures were instituted, but clinical instability persisted until rescue intravenous lipid emulsion (ILE) was administered.

pmc-13583446.title: Influence of Cellulose Particles on Streptomyces spp. Growth, Morphology, and Metabolite Spectrum
pmc-13583446.creator: Dorothea M. Schütterle, Bashar Al‐Smadi, Jethro L. Hemmann, Gesa Brauneck, Ana M. Palacio‐Barrera, Ivan Schlembach, Sascha Schäuble, Jorgen Barsett Magnus, Gianni Panagiotou, Miriam A. Rosenbaum
pmc-13583446.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Filamentous soil bacteria of the genus Streptomyces are a major source of bioactive natural products, including antibiotics. However, their industrial cultivation is complicated by complex morphologies ranging from dispersed mycelia to dense pellets, which are closely linked to productivity. Microparticles, such as talc or aluminium oxide, are commonly added to modulate macromorphology, yet their effects across diverse Streptomyces species remain insufficiently characterized.
